Key observations from the test image:
- Dead/dying soybean plant at soil line showing root/stem damage
- Brown-gray rotted root tissue
- **Distinctive blue-green spore masses** on the taproot surface
- Severely rotted root system

The blue-green spores on the taproot are a hallmark diagnostic feature of **Sudden Death Syndrome**. Let me confirm with reference images.
The SDS reference image (bottom-left) matches almost identically — rotted taproot with blue-green fungal growth visible on the root surface. Let me check one more candidate.

Phytophthora shows soft brown stem rot without the blue-green spore masses seen in the test image.

**Conclusion:** The test image shows a soybean taproot with the pathognomonic **blue-green spore masses** (Fusarium virguliforme conidia) on the root surface, combined with severe root rot and plant death — all perfectly matching Sudden Death Syndrome. The SDS reference collage (bottom-left panel) is nearly identical to the test image.
